Let D be weakly connected and acyclic with missing source-sink pair (s,t), and let J be a dijoin of the passive completion D+(s->t). If H=D+reverse(J) is not strongly connected, its condensation has unique source containing t and unique sink containing s. For F subset A minus J, J union F is an original dijoin iff s reaches t in D+reverse(J union F). The minimum size of such F equals the shortest s-t path cost with original and already-selected reversals free and every other unit-arc reversal of cost one.

routes.retired_because: This was an unspecified initial campaign placeholder. The live operator target is now recorded precisely by ONEFILL3256 and UNIT_VIA_WEIGHTED3256, with a source-corrected boundary; retiring this placeholder is not a mathematical exclusion of general counterexample searches.

Adding a zero-capacity arc between incomparable endpoints can remove original dicuts: two unit parallel arcs x->z and two y->z admit completion packings consisting only of x->z arcs, which miss the original dicut at y. This kills unrestricted completion lifting, not Woodall equality.
Reachability-redundant completion proves only the comparable-terminal subcase; the live objective explicitly requires incomparable endpoints as well.
A weighted Edmonds-Giles counterexample with zero-capacity arcs cannot be converted to an all-unit counterexample merely by deleting those arcs: deletion changes dicut topology.

The present core postcondition alone has not established a qualifying new contribution. The weighted one-fill equality is explicitly subsumed by the statement of Floros version 1.0 Theorem 1.1; the transfers and unrestricted reconstruction are prior mechanisms; no new packing consequence, improved bound, or independently verified publishable value of the remaining geometric observation has been supplied. Retiring this qualification attempt does not refute the sound proof, certify the competing proposed proof, or exclude future materially different applications.

The initial obligation ALIGN_SINGLE3256 merely restated the full desired coloring and did not isolate the gap. It is replaced by SINGLE_SPLIT3256, which separates the proved tight-exceptional-cut subcase from the unresolved strict-slack case. This is a decomposition refinement, not a refutation of existential color alignment.

The exact q=3 four-vertex construction partitions all nine unit arcs into completion dijoins, but two colors miss the original exceptional x->y cut. There are no unassigned arcs, so preserving all color assignments and adding arcs cannot repair the packing. This excludes additions-only lifting of arbitrary prescribed completion packings; it does not exclude recoloring or refute Woodall packing.

The exact five-vertex eleven-unit-arc construction has a dijoin J and a disjoint two-dijoin in the original topology, but deleting J makes u a sink and leaves s unable to reach both y and t. Therefore arbitrary P1 deletion does not preserve the one-defect class. No assertion is made about a specially chosen structurally preserving dijoin.

The simple K_(q+1,q+1) minus s->t family is in the exact terminal-minimum-cut strict-slack regime but every P1-type dijoin deletion creates at least q+2 missing pairs. The q=3 exact replay checks all 32768 arc subsets and 522 P1-type dijoins; minimum residual defects is five. This kills existentially chosen class-preserving P1 recursion, not packing.

In the exact fourteen-unit-arc strict-slack example, the bad color has a shortest repair of cost one, but each possible bridging donor loses its only arc at a source or sink. All 28 single recolorings are rejected, whereas a two-arc swap gives a full packing. Therefore donor-safe one-arc descent does not hold; the single-color path criterion alone is insufficient.

The initial route did not explicitly carry the reviewed minimum-counterexample reduction needed to apply a terminal-minimum-cut lifting premise to the wider strict-slack goal. GLOBAL_SBO_FULL_ROUTE_SINGLE3256 records that prerequisite. This is a decomposition correction, not a refutation of structure-aware strong base orderability.

The all-q K_(q+1,q+1) minus s->t strict-slack family has 2q+2 vertices, whereas any all-unit sink-regular (q,q+1)-bipartite graph retaining at most one missing pair has at most 2q+1. Literal contraction cannot increase vertex count. Strongly base orderable lifts with many missing pairs remain unresolved and are not refuted.

Its cut counts are 2+0=1+1, so the tight gluing contradiction is unavailable. The graph is packable; only automatic coverage from prescribed aligned boundary colors is excluded.

The earlier 282 positive cases imposed all-terminal degree two and strict reserved nonterminal cuts, which do not hold for general reserved pairs. Retire the universal local rule, not the full packing target.

This retires exposure plus the existing Schrijver minimal-block extension, not the existential reserved theorem or a different construction imposing additional ordinary constraints.

The two remaining reserved terminal units s->y and b->Nb must have equal colors, but induced R in color zero requires s->y color zero and induced L in color one requires b->Nb color one. All 128 terminal-component assignments fail those simultaneous induced-region demands. The original reviewed reserved pair is packable. Retire the stronger separated-region existence criterion, not its valid sufficient implication or the exact reserved-pair theorem.
